question: When the sandbox dies mid-review, or a round follows earlier Kody suggestions on the same PR, does what reaches the PR match what a correct review delivers — nothing unread, revisions linked, nothing already sent posted again?

cases.checks: Kody Rule on a file new in the PR; the developer answered with a comment that documents nothing; stored implemented; 15 earlier comments
Kody Rule "regenerate, do not hand-edit" on a generated API client; the hand-edited line it flagged was edited by hand again this round; stored not_implemented; 10 earlier comments
Kody Rule (no magic literals for units and quantities) on a Go file new in the PR; stored not_implemented; more than 40 later comments push the earlier one out of the history
Bug finder; a skip check runs before the title it tests is assigned, so it never matches; the developer extracted the check into a helper and kept the order; stored implemented; 44 earlier comments
Finder (Ruby): applying the earlier suggestion (implemented) introduced a new, different bug in a caller; must be posted and linked to the suggestion it revises; 3 earlier comments

WHY: the 5s timeout is a no-op and getJson still hangs forever on a server that never answers, which is exactly the failure the timeout was added to prevent. HOW: pass the signal: `const res = await fetch(url, { signal: controller.signal });`.
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed: line 5 calls `fetch(url)` with no options, so the AbortController's signal is never wired to the request. `controller.abort()` at line 3 therefore has no effect and the 5s timeout cannot cancel a hanging fetch, defeating the timeout's purpose. This is a concrete, verified bug, not style. It is a distinct problem from the previous suggestion (which only asked to add a timeout) — the timeout was added but is ineffective, so this is a new bug in the applied fix, not a repeat.

The claim asserts buildEntries produces entries whose scope is the empty string for non-conventional titles (e.g. `feat: x`), which then render under an empty `### ` heading. HOW: guard the match and default the scope to something stable, e.g. `const match = /^\w+\(([^)]+)\):/.exec(title); return match?.[1] ?? 'other';` (and drop the unsound cast).
verificationEvidence.rationale: Confirmed. The claimed failure path is real and reachable. Not covered by any prior decision (which concern other files/rules), and it is not a style issue.

HOW: have renew_due rescue the not-found case and continue, e.g. wrap the body in `begin ... rescue SubscriptionNotFound ... next end` (or provide a non-raising lookup such as `@repo.find_by(id: id)` for the batch path) so one missing subscription does not stop the loop.

In renew_due that raises SubscriptionNotFound, aborting the `ids.each` loop and skipping all remaining valid subscriptions in the batch. The finding's root cause and failure path are concrete and correct. Note: this is a distinct consequence from the earlier round-a-P41 decision, which asked find_subscription to raise (to protect charge_now); the batch caller renew_due was not addressed by that change and now silently loses the skip semantics it relied on.
